column1: # Shared oracle (#1023), measured with Java at the low-level Classic entry, parse(context, kind, false), after a
# prefix of prefixCP code points of input "<prefix>c" (snapshot ba28bed2). The shapes put a rule whose body is only a
# rule reference (`Rule[Rule[X]]`: rule 1 with body Expr::Rule(2), a Java single-element LazyChain) where
# conformance/owned-capture-virtual/classic.tsv has none. Such a rule returns its own collection, as
# Rule[Chain[Rule[X]]] (the UBNF form, Expr::Sequence[Rule]) does, not the source its inner rule returned: generated
# "" in the virtual kinds, the empty input at the cursor for a consumed collection of a MatchOnly token or of a
# selected generated child. A Choice of a rule reference still returns the selected child's Parsed (the controls
# Rule[Choice[Rule[..],q]], Choice[Rule[..]]). Every row holds for Memoization x Diagnostics (6 options).
# provenance/startCP/endCP/text: Java NamedCapture("v", ..) (~ = empty); consumed/matched: the cursor after it. The
# predicate at the same entry sees the same value: accepted with candidate text@startCP when INPUT, else rejected
# the token of the generated UBNF @f site (__CaptureSite) at its raw offsets, - when rejected; it is accepted exactly
# when input is, with the cursor of the owned entry, and a rejection leaves the cursor at the prefix.
# rust is "=" when Rust agrees, else the Rust owned value: a known #1023 D difference (the virtualTokenConsumed
# collection of generated "g" keeps its text, and the gen0 anchor), the same as for Chain[genc:g] and Rule[genc:g].
